question.text: The Ming dynasty was established after the Red Turban rebellions that overthrew this Chinese successor dynasty to the Mongol Empire. Marco Polo's writings about China were during the time of this dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Yuan Dynasty [do not accept or prompt on "Mongol Dynasty"]
question.clue: It established its capital at Cambaluc , now modern day Beijing.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about dynasties of China.
swap.text: This last imperial dynasty of China was overthrown by the Xinhai ["sheen-hi"] Revolution. This dynasty fought the Opium Wars with Great Britain and the Sino-Japanese wars with Japan.
swap.clue: This dynasty's "century of humiliation" resulted after it was forced to sign a sequence of "unequal treaties'" marking its defeat in the Opium Wars.

question.leadin: This event's "Down to the Countryside" Movement sent youth from cities to farms, resulting in a "lost generation." --.
question.text: Identify this movement that targeted the "four olds." The "Gang of Four" became prominent during this period that attempted to purge any remaining elements of capitalism from a certain country.
question.clue: This period saw many "big-character" posters, the first of which was created by Nie Yuanzi, and the Four Olds were attacked, leading to the loss of many artifacts and historical records.

swap.text: The construction of over six thousand backyard steel furnaces was a part of this economic policy by which Mao planned for China to modernize in a short period of time.
swap.answerHtml: Great Leap Forward [also accept Second Five-Year Plan or Dayuejin]
swap.clue: Millions of people were encouraged to set up backyard furnaces during this campaign.

question.leadin: This man was given his new surname by the Yongle emperor.
question.text: Name this Muslim eunuch who was comissioned to go on seven "treasure voyages" in the oceans south of China, ranging all the way to Africa. His ships were the largest wooden ships ever built.
question.clue: This diplomat was given a giraffe and a zebra while taking tribute from Malindi and the Swahili coast.

swap.leadin: After refusing to respond to Japanese incursions, this man was kidnapped by two subordinates and forced to ally with his political opponents in the Xi'an [shee an] Incident.
swap.text: Name this leader who reunified China during the Warlord Era.
swap.answerHtml: Chiang Kai-Shek [or Jiang Jieshi; or Chiang Chungcheng; prompt on partial answers that do not include the underlined portion]
swap.clue: This man was appointed as Commandant of the Whampoa military academy in 1924.

question.leadin: This dynasty's Southern period began after its emperor was captured and its capital, Kaifeng, sacked by invading Jurchens.
question.text: Name this dynasty, which followed the Tang Dynasty and was supplanted by Kublai Khan's Yuan Dynasty. This dynasty was the first to use gunpowder.
question.clue: Bi Sheng worked under this dynasty, which switched lines of succession due to the Jingkang Incident.

swap.text: This man was the first president of the Republic of China, and lived in Japan during his exile.
swap.clue: Though he was educated in Hawaii, he was in exile in Japan when he formed the Tongmenghui society.

question.leadin: Answer the following about China's last emperor, P'u Yi.
question.text: P'u Yi lived his young life in this complex, not leaving until he was forced to in 1924. Aside from royals, the only males allowed in the inner palace were court eunuchs.
question.clue: The earth removed in the construction of the moat around this place was used to create Jingshan Hill, the place where the Chongzhen Emperor committed suicide.

swap.text: Opium had first started coming into China during the rule of the Yongzheng Emperor, the son of this man. This second Qing emperor is credited with opening China to the West, and he faced the Revolt of the Three Feudatories during his reign.
swap.clue: This man removed his first-born son Yinreng from succession and imprisoned him .

question.leadin: The Nazi John Rabe formed a "safety zone" that sheltered about twenty thousand would-be victims of this event.
question.text: Name this atrocity during which Japanese forces slaughtered over one hundred thousand Chinese civilians living in the namesake city.
question.clue: One infamous incident during this event was the "kill one hundred people with a sword contest" that was "won" by Toshaki Mukai.

swap.leadin: This scholar was forced to choose between execution and castration for defending Li Ling after Li was captured by the Xiongnu ("sh'yung-noo").
swap.text: Name this thinker who accepted castration in order to finish his magnum opus, Records of the Grand Historian, which covers 2500 years of Chinese history.
swap.clue: This court eunuch wrote a biography of emperors starting with Huangdi, also known as the Yellow Emperor, to his contemporary Emperor Wu of Han.

question.text: After passing the final Metropolitan Exam, candidates were awarded this highest and final degree. The purchasing of this degree toward the end of the Qing (ching) meant the "Imperial Scholars" who held it were no longer guaranteed the highest offices.
question.clue: Successful candidates in the civil service exams were awarded this degree title. From the reign of the Ming emperor Yingzong ("EENG-DZONG"), only holders of this title were permitted into the Hanlin Academy.

swap.text: This Christian convert claimed that he was the younger brother of Jesus and led the Taiping rebellion.
swap.clue: He was succeeded upon his death by his son Tianguifu , whereupon the body of this man who claimed to be the brother of Jesus Christ was further damaged by a commander of the Everlasting army, Zeng Guofan.

question.text: The Revolt of the Three Feudatories occurred during the reign of this Qing emperor, who also dealt with the Chinese Rites controversy.
question.clue: During the regency of Oboi, he ordered the evacuation of Guangdong in the Great Clearance as part of his campaign against Koxinga (koh-SHIN-gah).

swap.leadin: These objects were produced by heating scapulae and plastrons.
swap.text: Name these organic objects used for divination, the source of the earliest known Chinese writing.
swap.clue: The so-called "Waste of Yin" was an important site for the collection of these items, which sometimes bore messages about toothache, the success of deer-hunting, or appropriate dates for the birth of a child.

question.leadin: Legends about the circumstances surrounding this man's rise to power include the "golden shelf promise" and the "sound of the axe in the shadow of the flickering candle."
question.text: Name this man who ruled from 976 to 997 and extinguished the Northern Han to bring to a final end the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms.
question.clue: The "Incident at Xuanwu Gate" saw this ruler take power by ambushing and killing his brother Li Jiangcheng. This ruler succeeded Gaozu, or Li Yuan, as the second emperor of the Tang Dynasty.

swap.leadin: The Mongol invasion of China subjugated this northern kingdom whose own invasion of China had led to the formation of the Southern Song.
swap.text: Name this dynasty founded by the Jurchens, whose name literally means "gold" in Chinese.
swap.clue: The next masters of the northern Chinese frontier were this dynasty, which overthrew the Liao and ruled from 1115 to 1234, when their capital of Kaifeng fell. They banned all Chinese culture from their army in an attempt to preserve their ethnic identity.

question.text: Peaceful "wo lei fei" in Hong Kong often participate in protests by performing this action. A controversial law passed in June 2020 made it a crime to lodge "insults" when this action was taking place in Hong Kong.
question.answerHtml: singing [accept answers like singing the official or unofficial national anthem; accept playing a national anthem]
question.clue: The Baltic countries gained independence from the Soviet Union in a "revolution" named for this action. That revolution named for this action included the formation of a human chain across all three countries.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the state of Wei after Cao Cao's death.
swap.text: Members of this clan served as regents of the Wei state starting with Yi. Another member of this clan named Qian, wrote the Records of the Grand Historian.
swap.clue: The Three Rebellions in Shouchun began after one member of this clan usurped the regency for Cao Shuang from the Cao clan during the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs.
